purpose: Exact declared architecture-debt ledger. Each entry enumerates concrete file paths for a dependency-direction violation that the target boundary policy forbids and that is live at the baseline named by its own source_sha. This ledger is not an allowlist: reconciliation asserts exact set equality against the live scan, so an undeclared equivalent violation, a new importer, a different path, a value-edge upgrade, or a stale entry all fail. An entry declares one source and the exact targets it reaches; the declared key set is the cross product, so a partially closed entry surfaces as stale and must be split by a human rather than silently shrinking.

baselines.066a43c3df07f3da10a2fc93ff7d90157c732114: WU-00 refactor base. Entries carrying this sha were live before the architecture program began.
baselines.3a2bf3cbbffd304d7db4a0eb5a7d5058ae2d3402: WU-A enforcement baseline. Entries carrying this sha were first observable as a violation of a policy WU-A installed, at a source path that did not exist at the refactor base.

debts.risk: The inbox use case selects concrete provider implementations itself, through a switch over six value imports. Activating a real provider is therefore an edit to an application-layer file, and the layer transitively reads process.env, because resolveGitHubClient() is called with no arguments and reads GITHUB_SOURCE_MODE, GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN and NODE_ENV directly. The coupling is not new work: the identical six imports were live at the refactor base in app/api/workunit/inbox/route.ts, and WU-02S relocated them into the application layer when it split the read and refresh paths. The source path is therefore younger than the defect, and the source_sha records where the edge is observed rather than claiming it originated there.
debts.removal_gate: The use case consumes an injected signal-source port instead of importing provider modules, and the concrete provider set is selected outside the application layer. The program still records provider integration as open under WU-02: the executed WU-02 slice was the dependency-direction closure of the normalized signal contract only, and explicitly did not authorize or implement canonical source adapters or provider integration.
